thread:
support_elaine: Hey @sre_oncall — acme-prod is reporting a spike of 503s starting ~08:12 UTC. Ticket: https://redwood.support/t/ACME-921. Customers see timeouts and 500/503 responses.

sre_oncall: looking. any correlation with deploys? @deploy-bot did anything go out around 08:00? :eyes: 

deploy-bot: deploy activity: no user-facing deploys to hosted-infer during 07:30-08:30 UTC. Autoscaler triggered a node add at 07:58.

support_elaine: customer says errors mostly on long-context requests (context ~6k tokens) and heavy tool-calls.

infra_mike: pulling logs from the upstream runner pool for acme routing tag. running: `kubectl -n hosted logs -l app=infer-runner -c runner --since=30m` now. initial grep shows repeated `segfault`/`illegal instruction` in some pods followed by OOMKilled containers. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T08:11:45Z] worker-7c9b4fd segfault at 0 ip 00007f3b7a2...
[2026-03-17T08:11:46Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 23456 (infer-runne) total-vm:12000000kB
[2026-03-17T08:11:46Z] ContainerRestartCount: 3
```

ml_li: that pattern matches a GPU memory spiral we've seen when large context + batchsize + prefetch hit kv-cache prefetching. Could be kv prefault blowing past cgroup limits then segfault.

sre_oncall: can you check `nvidia-smi` timelines and dmesg from the node where worker-7c9b4fd ran? Also `coredumpctl` if core saved.

infra_mike: `nvidia-smi` shows persistent memory bump and single GPU hitting 100% mem then process killed. dmesg shows repeated page-fault GPU resets. coredumpctl didn't capture (container restarted too fast).

support_elaine: customer shows request samples and curl repro. short sample: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <tok>" -d '{"model":"gpt-large-8k", "input": "<6k tokens>", "max_tokens":1024, "batch_size":8}'`

ml_li: repro idea: run a local stress with identical context + concurrency 6-8 to reproduce. Also try forcing `PREFETCH_KV=false` to see if kv prefetch is the culprit.

sre_oncall: immediate mitigation: add routing rule to fallback to smaller model variant (gpt-medium- context-optimized) for Acme to avoid large-kv path, and temporarily cap concurrency for hosted route to 2. Can ops add fallback ASAP?

infra_mike: added a temporary routing override: `routes.acme-prod.fallback_model = gpt-medium-4k` and `routes.acme-prod.max_concurrency = 2` — pushed 08:25 UTC. Watch on telemetry.

support_elaine: customer reports errors dropping after 08:28, success rate improving. :thumbsup:

ml_li: for root cause — we need a repro build. @infra_mike can you snapshot the node filesystem and get the last container logs and `gdb` stack if core appears next time? Steps I want in writeup: 
1) Collect full runner logs: `kubectl -n hosted logs <pod> -c runner --previous --timestamps`
2) Capture GPU state: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1` during repro
3) Enable `PREFETCH_KV=false` and repro load to see if memory plateau differs
4) If segfault again, run `host coredumpctl dump <pid> > /tmp/core.$PID` and attach to ticket

infra_mike: noted. I'll spin up an isolated reproducer cluster with the same model binary + quantization flags and run Li's stress script.

sre_oncall: also adding a temporary alert: if runner OOMKill rate > 2 within 5m for a routing tag, trigger automated fallback to cold-standby model. Config change in progress.

support_elaine: customer wants ETA on permanent fix — can we estimate?

ml_li: depends on root cause; if it's kv-prefetch memory leak under certain token distributions we'll need patch in runtime (2-3 days for hotfix + testing). If it's quantization kernel misbehaving, might be 1-2 weeks. We'll prioritize.

infra_mike: filed internal repro ticket INF-7832 and attached initial logs. linking to customer ticket.

support_elaine: great, keeping customer updated. closing loop here once INF-7832 has reproducible steps. thanks everyone.

deploy-bot: automated note: routing override applied and alert created at 08:26:12 UTC.

customer_acme_bot: ACME ticket updated: temporary fallback applied; monitoring. Thank you.
